core.title: Responsive width conditions use only the declared breakpoints
core.given: A style artifact of the presentation layer, outside vendored and generated trees, contains a responsive width condition (a condition on layout width; the construct and its forms come from the profile). The stack declares its responsive widths in one place: the breakpoints width conditions may use, and the viewports responsive specs render at; both declaration locations come from the profile.
core.when: Any responsive width condition in scope exists or is added or changed, or the breakpoint declaration is edited so that existing conditions must be re-checked.
core.then: Every width in every in-scope responsive width condition MUST be one of the declared breakpoints (breakpoint declaration from the profile); a width counts as a declared breakpoint under the stack's width-matching rules (tolerance below a breakpoint and unit conversion, from the profile).
prefer: During GREEN: reuse an existing declared breakpoint that expresses the required layout transition.
During GREEN: add one breakpoint to the breakpoint declaration only when the current design genuinely requires a distinct transition width.
During GREEN: change only the affected width condition or configuration entry.
avoid: Using an undeclared one-off width as a shortcut.
Adding speculative breakpoints for future devices.
Normalizing unrelated responsive rules while fixing this one.
unless: The file lives in a vendored or generated tree; these are never scanned.
core.why: Declaring the breakpoints once and requiring every width condition to use them keeps layouts switching at the same widths everywhere instead of at a new one per component.
evidence: Every affected width condition is declared (the stack's responsive-width check reports no finding).
The current responsive acceptance test passes at the relevant viewports (the widths responsive specs render at, from the profile).
verification: The check examines every width condition in every in-scope style artifact, in every form the stack's styling supports (forms from the profile), and compares each width against the declared breakpoints (declaration from the profile).
A width counts as a declared breakpoint only under the stack's width-matching rules, tolerance below a breakpoint and unit conversion, applied exactly as the profile states them.

Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; the exact classification of which trees count as vendored or generated for this check is owned by this rule's own checker (a realization detail). The check defers to that classification and does not redefine the stack-wide excluded-roots list for this rule.

The obligation covers every width condition in scope, including pre-existing and unchanged ones; conditions that carry no width condition (for example user-preference or output-medium conditions) are not covered, and the file kind alone cannot establish that a width condition exists, only the content check can.
Severity 3; disposition strict: an undeclared width is always reported.

values: style artifacts: standalone stylesheets and component source files that may carry style blocks or styling-in-code (kinds from the profile)
file content contains a responsive width condition (construct from the profile)
the repository configuration file that carries the breakpoint declaration (from the profile); edits to it can invalidate existing width conditions anywhere in scope
responsive width condition added or modified
breakpoint declaration entry added, removed or changed
undeclared breakpoint: a width condition in scope (including pre-existing ones) whose width is not a declared breakpoint

fires: A style artifact adds a width condition whose width is not in the breakpoint declaration.
A width condition in any supported form (bounded-below, bounded-above, range) uses an undeclared width.
A bounded-above width condition is neither a declared breakpoint nor within the matching tolerance below one.
An existing, unchanged width condition at a previously declared width is left in place after that width is removed from the breakpoint declaration.
A pre-existing width condition in scope uses an undeclared width (the obligation covers every width condition, not only newly written ones).
doesNotFire: A width condition uses a width that equals a declared breakpoint, or matches one under the stack's width-matching rules (a bounded-above value within tolerance below a declared breakpoint, or a relative-unit value that converts to one).
A width condition lives in a vendored or generated tree (never scanned).
A styling condition carries no width condition (for example a user-preference or output-medium condition).

profileRequirements.meaning: How a width in a condition is matched to a declared breakpoint: the tolerance below a breakpoint and unit conversion.
profileRequirements.bunValue: A `max-width` X matches breakpoint B when X == B or B-1 <= X < B (within 1px below, e.g. `767px`, `767.98px` for 768); `em`/`rem` convert to px at 16px before matching

profileRequirements.meaning: The repository configuration file in which the breakpoint and viewport declarations live.

proposedKeys.meaning: How a width in a condition is matched to a declared breakpoint: the tolerance below a breakpoint and unit conversion applied before matching.
proposedKeys.bunValue: A `max-width` X matches breakpoint B when X == B or B-1 <= X < B (within 1px below, e.g. `767px`, `767.98px` for 768); `em`/`rem` convert to px at 16px before matching
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: Width-equivalence semantics of the stack's styling are an idiom with no existing key; no other group describes value matching.

bunOnly.text: CSS custom properties cannot be used in media queries, so breakpoints cannot be tokens.
bunOnly.reason: This is a limitation of CSS media queries specifically; styling systems in other stacks can reference shared design tokens or constants in width conditions, so the token-inability rationale has no stack-neutral equivalent. The core keeps only the neutral rationale: one declaration keeps layouts switching at the same widths everywhere.

neutralityNotes: The exact width-condition syntax (min-width/max-width and range forms), the breakpoint and viewport declaration locations with their defaults, and the width-matching rules (1px-below tolerance, em/rem at 16px) have no stack-neutral phrasing; they are carried as profile values (five proposed idiom keys, since the closed vocabulary has no styling keys), so the instantiated core imposes exactly the Bun obligation. Two parts are deliberately kept in the realization rather than generalized: (1) the rationale that CSS width conditions cannot reference design tokens is a CSS-specific limitation, so the core rationale covers only consistent layout transition widths; (2) the exact vendored/generated-tree classification (node_modules, dist, build, _generated) is owned by this rule's own checker and is not the stack-wide excluded-roots union, so core verification defers to the checker's classification instead of using roots.excluded. Detector id and provenance stay bunOnly per the notProfileKeys list. The path_glob activation facts could not be expressed as neutral activation facts (the fact vocabulary has no path type): the exclusion moved to verification with checker-owned classification, and the config-file trigger is kept as a file_kind fact over roots.config. 'During GREEN' is retained as ATDD phase terminology. Concrete numeric examples were kept out of the core's fires/doesNotFire in favor of role-level statements, because bun.json itself is delivered as the worked reference example.
